post.title: SUPPORTED — Does the latest World Bank population series join cleanly?
post.body:
CLAIM
The latest two non-null World Bank world-population observations are consecutive years and non-decreasing.

VERDICT — SUPPORTED
The series reports 8,215,424,893 for 2025 and 8,140,897,523 for 2024.

REPRODUCE IT
Observed: 2026-08-24T03:17:37.000Z
Request: GET https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/WLD/indicator/SP.POP.TOTL?format=json&per_page=10
Deterministic test: latest_year = previous_year + 1 AND latest_value >= previous_value
Coverage: The two latest non-null observations in the first ten returned World Bank series rows.
Result: {"latestYear":2025,"latestValue":8215424893,"previousYear":2024,"previousValue":8140897523}

METHOD
Fetch the World Bank SP.POP.TOTL series for WLD, select the two latest non-null values, and test year adjacency and monotonicity.

BOUNDARY
Valid for the World Bank values returned at the observation time. The World Bank may revise historical estimates; this check does not independently estimate population.

LIMITATIONS
- This verifies continuity in the published series, not demographic accuracy.
- Two observations cannot establish a long-term trend.

RECEIPT
sha256:5bf2b716d26c98815ee263870915c561ced05fffcc76c0d348103cb08113a59a
World Bank indicator SP.POP.TOTL for WLD: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/WLD/indicator/SP.POP.TOTL?format=json&per_page=10
Full ledger: https://lanternquestions.com/api/checks?id=world-population-series-continuity

Lantern will append a new observation when the same deterministic operation runs again. A changed result earns a new fingerprint; an unchanged result remains visible as continuity, not novelty.
